```{r, include=FALSE}
get_mode <- function(x) {

}
```

## Data import and sample summary

We used repeated photographs from an individually marked breeding population at Kaikoura to ask how the expression of the rufous breast band and the timing of its post-breeding molt varies with sex, age, migratory strategy, and breeding phenology. Our full dataset spanned three breeding seasons and was linked to an individual's breeding records and (if known) their age and migratory status. This section loads the full dataset used throughout the markdown and gives a brief summary of seasonal coverage and sample size before proceeding to the hypotheses and predictions, analysis, and results.

```{r}
dat_breeding <-
  readRDS(
    here("data/moult_breeding_KK_data.rds")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rings_comb_raw = as.character(rings_comb),
    rings_comb = rings_comb_simp
  )

# Use one season-specific centering/scaling rule throughout the qmd so
# t0 and k remain comparable across model subsets.
date_scaling_ref <- dat_breeding %>%
  distinct(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(
    date_J_mean_ref = mean(date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    date_J_sd_ref = sd(date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

add_reference_date_scaling <- function(data, date_col = "date_J") {
  data %>%
    left_join(date_scaling_ref, by = "season") %>%
    mutate(
      date_J_scaled = (.data[[date_col]] - date_J_mean_ref) / date_J_sd_ref
    )
}
```

For all analyses below, `rings_comb` is the simplified individual identifier (`rings_comb_simp`), while the original raw notation is retained as `rings_comb_raw`. This collapses duplicated raw codes such as `RBLY`/`RBLY_F`, `RBYG`/`RBYG_F`, and `RRYY`/`RRYY_F` to the same biological individual.

We first summarise the number of photographs and the date range covered
in each season.

```{r, echo= FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(n_obs = n(),
            min_date = min(date),
            max_date = max(date))
```

We then count the number of individuals represented in the full
photographic dataset.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  pull(rings_comb) %>% unique() %>% length()
```

Finally, we check how many individuals were sampled in more than one
season, because repeated sampling across years is what allows us to
estimate persistent individual differences.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  select(rings_comb, season) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(rings_comb) %>%
  summarise(n_seasons = n()) %>%
  group_by(n_seasons) %>%
  summarise(n())
```

total, mean, and SD of photos for each individual per season
```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  group_by(rings_comb, season) %>%
  summarise(n_photos = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(total_photo = sum(n_photos),
         mean_photos_per_ind_per_season = mean(n_photos),
         sd_photos_per_ind_per_season = sd(n_photos)) %>%
  distinct(total_photo, mean_photos_per_ind_per_season, sd_photos_per_ind_per_season)
```

max and min number of photos per individual per season
```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  group_by(rings_comb, season) %>%
  summarise(n_photos = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(sum_n = sum(n_photos),
         mean_n = mean(n_photos),
         sd_n = sd(n_photos)) %>%
  summarise(max_photos_ind_season = max(n_photos),
            min_photos_ind_season = min(n_photos))
```

### Table of scored photos
Note, in the analysed dataset, for a given individual, each date had only one score, hence the larger sample shown in this table.

#### Variable definitions

- <code>sourcefile</code>: the directory path to the original photo scored from Ailsa's catalogue
- <code>rings_comb_raw</code>: the original 4-band code in the raw dataset, including occasional duplicate notations for the same bird
- <code>rings_comb</code>: the simplified individual identifier used throughout the analyses (`rings_comb_simp`)
- <code>score</code>: the score of the rufous breast band according to the 1-7 scheme shown below
- <code>date</code>: the date of the photo (extracted from the photo's metadata)
- <code>date_J</code>: the Julian date of the photo, shifted to have an July 1 origin for the autral summer
- <code>sex</code>: sex based on plumage (M or F)
- <code>season</code>: breeding season of the given photo
- <code>migratory_status</code>: Resident (R) or migrant (M) classified from satellite tracking and/or winter resightings
- <code>age</code>: known age in years at the time of the photo (only available for those that were banded locally as chicks and recruited)
- <code>first_date_breeding_final</code>: first date seen incubating (raw date)
- <code>last_date_breeding_final</code>: last date seen incubating or brooding (raw date)
- <code>last_nest_first_obs</code>: initiation date of last nest (raw date)
- <code>first_breeding_date_J_snum</code>: first date seen incubating (season scaled Julian date, shifted for austral summer)
- <code>last_breeding_date_J_snum</code>: last date seen incubating or brooding (season scaled Julian date, shifted for austral summer)
- <code>last_nest_first_obs_J_snum</code>: initiation date of last nest (season scaled Julian date, shifted for austral summer)

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  select(
    sourcefile, rings_comb_raw, rings_comb, score, date, date_J, sex, season, migratory_status, age,
    first_date_breeding_final, last_date_breeding_final,
    first_breeding_date_J_snum, last_breeding_date_J_snum
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(first_date_breeding_final, last_date_breeding_final),
      ~ as.Date(., origin = "1970-01-01")
    )
  ) %>%
  datatable(
    class = "cell-border stripe",
    rownames = FALSE,
    filter = "top"
  ) %>%
  formatRound(
    columns = c(
      "last_breeding_date_J_snum",
      "first_breeding_date_J_snum"
    ),
    digits = 2
  )
```

## Hypotheses and predictions
We tested the following five hypotheses. The 'Sex' and 'Breeding phenology' models used the full dataset, while the 'Age class', 'Continuous age', and 'Migratory status' models used subsets of the full dataset for individuals of known age or migratory status (see Table 1 for sample sizes).

### Sex
- H1: sexual dichromatism in the rufous band score and sex-specific molt timing
- P1a: males tend to have higher rufous band scores than females, following the general patter of moderate sexual dichromatism in other Charadriidae plovers
- P1b: no difference in post-breeding molt timing due to the socially monogamous and bi-parental care mating system

### Breeding phenology
- H2: post-breeding molt is dependent upon breeding phenology
- P2a: individuals that breed earlier molt earlier due a generally more advanced reproductive schedule
- P2b: individuals that are still engaged in parental care late in the season molt later
- P2c: individuals that initiate late nests molt later

### Age class
- H3: age-class structures the molt schedule and rufous band expression
- P3a: first-year birds express lower rufous band scores in comparison to after-first-year birds due to more complete pigmentation during feather growth in older birds
- P3b: first-year birds molt earlier than after-first-year birds because the flight feathers of first-years are older (and more worn) than after-first-years, which triggers an earlier complete post-breeding molt program

### Continuous age
- H4: beyond the first-year transition continuous age structures the molt schedule and rufous band expression
- P4a: no age-dependent variation in rufous band expression (either within or between individuals)
- P4b: no age-dependent variation in post-breeding molt timing (either within or between individuals)

### Migratory strategy
- H5: migratory strategy structures the molt schedule and rufous band expression
- P5a: no strategy-dependent variation in rufous band expression
- P5b: migrants molt earlier than residents due to their more constrained fall migration schedule

## Non-linear mixed effects model

We scored the rufous breast band on a seven-point scale, so the response is bounded and declines through the season as birds transition from their breeding ("alternate") plumage into their non-breeding plumage ("basic") via the complete post-breeding molt.

We fit the same nonlinear trajectory for all five models and let the predictors explain variation in the starting score and the timing of the decline.

We modeled the decline in rufous band score with a nonlinear mixed-effects curve. Because we centered and scaled Julian date within season before fitting, we write the seasonal date term as $x$. For observation $j$ on bird $i$,

$$
y_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_{ij}, \sigma).
$$

$$
\mu_{ij} =
1 + (\beta_{ij} - 1)
\left(
1 - \frac{1}{1 + \exp[-k(x_{ij} - t_{0,ij})]}
\right).
$$

The parameter $\beta$ is the rufous band score prior to the post-breeding molt, $t_0$ is the midpoint of the decline to the non-breeding plumage, and $k$ controls how steep/fast the molt progresses. Early in the season ($x \ll t_0$), expected scores are close to $\beta$; late in the season ($x \gg t_0$), expected scores approach 1 (i.e. full non-breeding plumage). This function attempts to match the biology of post-breeding moult, in which birds move from full breeding plumage toward full non-breeding plumage over time.

In the sex-specific model, we allowed both $\beta$ and $t_0$ to depend on sex and to vary among birds and bird-by-season combinations, while keeping $k$ common across birds (i.e., our photographic sampling was too coarse to robustly assess sources of variation in molt speed):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_{ij} &= \alpha_{\beta} + \mathbf{X}_{ij}\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{\beta} + b_{\beta,i} + b_{\beta,is}, \\
t_{0,ij} &= \alpha_{t_0} + \mathbf{X}_{ij}\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{t_0} + b_{t_0,i} + b_{t_0,is}, \\
k &= \alpha_k .
\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $\mathbf{X}$ denotes the relevant fixed effects for a given model. In the sex-only model, $\mathbf{X}$ contains sex; in the other models, we added breeding phenology, age class, continuous age terms (i.e., within- vs. between-individual), or migratory status. We kept the same nonlinear form throughout so that differences among models reflect changes in predictors of $\beta$ and $t_0$, not changes in the underlying molt curve.

We used an informative prior on $\beta$ (i.e., <code>normal(5.5, 1)</code>; centering the prior near the upper half of the 1-7 scoring scale and keeping it positive), weakly informative priors on $t_0$ and $k$, and exponential priors on the group-level standard deviations. This combination stabilized estimation while still allowing substantial variation among birds and among bird-by-season combinations when the data supported it.

The Figure 1 schematic below shows how $\beta$, $t_0$, and $k$ shape the curve that we fit in every model. We use representative values here so that the roles of the three parameters are easy to interpret.

### Figure 2 - schematic of the non-linear model
```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code of an example parameterizing the non-linear model"

# Draw a schematic version of the nonlinear curve used in all models.
# The values of beta, t0, and k are chosen for illustration only.

# Set the schematic parameters.
baseline <- 6
k <- 3.31
t0 <- 1.45

# Define the expected trajectory from the nonlinear model.
moult_mu <- function(x, baseline, k, t0) {
  1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (x - t0))))
}

# Build a clean x-range around the inflection point.
x <- seq(t0 - 2.5, t0 + 2.5, length.out = 600)

df <- tibble(
  x = x,
  mu = moult_mu(x, baseline = baseline, k = k, t0 = t0)
)

# At x = t0 the curve is halfway between the upper and lower asymptotes.
y_t0 <- moult_mu(t0, baseline = baseline, k = k, t0 = t0)

# The slope at t0 determines the tangent line used to illustrate k.
slope_t0 <- -(baseline - 1) * k / 4
angle_k <- atan(slope_t0) * 180 / pi

y_k <- 7
x_k <- t0 + (y_k - y_t0) / slope_t0
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show plotting code for the example"
fig1 <-
  ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = mu)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = baseline, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1, color = "grey70") +
  ggtext::geom_richtext(
    data = data.frame(x = min(df$x), y = baseline),
```

### Shared priors

We use the same prior set in all five non-linear moult models so that
differences among models reflect changes in predictors rather than
changes in prior assumptions. We define that shared prior set once here
and reuse it in each `brm()` call below.

```{r}
# Shared priors for all non-linear moult models.
moult_priors <- c(
  # The baseline score sits on the 1-7 scoring scale, so only the
  # baseline intercept is centered near the upper half of that range.
  prior(normal(5.5, 1), nlpar = "baseline", class = "b", coef = "Intercept"),
  # All non-intercept effects on baseline are treated as deviations from
  # that intercept and are therefore centered at zero.
  prior(normal(0, 1), nlpar = "baseline", class = "b"),

  # The inflection point is estimated on the season-standardized date
  # scale, so both the intercept and predictor effects are centered at zero.
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), nlpar = "t0", class = "b", coef = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), nlpar = "t0", class = "b"),

  # Positive values of k enforce the expected one-way seasonal decline.
  prior(normal(1, 0.5), nlpar = "k", lb = 0),

  # Group-level SDs are regularized, but can still be large if the data
  # support substantial heterogeneity among birds or bird-seasons.
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "baseline", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb"),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "baseline", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb:season"),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "t0", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb"),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "t0", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb:season")
)

# FY-only models do not include the nested bird-by-season random effect,
# so they need the corresponding subset of priors.
moult_priors_fy <- c(
  prior(normal(5.5, 1), nlpar = "baseline", class = "b", coef = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 1), nlpar = "baseline", class = "b"),
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), nlpar = "t0", class = "b", coef = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), nlpar = "t0", class = "b"),
  prior(normal(1, 0.5), nlpar = "k", lb = 0),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "baseline", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb"),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "t0", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb")
)
```

### Analysis: Sex-specific model
We first fit a model to the full dataset and asked whether males and females differed in $\beta$ and $t_0$. We used this as the reference model because sex was known for all birds and it gives the cleanest estimate of the post-breeding molt trajectory and baseline expression of the rufous band.

#### dataset
```{r}
# wrangle data
dat_sex_mod <- dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame()
```

#### model formula specification
```{r}
mod_sex <- bf(
  score ~ 1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0)))),
  baseline ~ sex + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  t0 ~ sex + season + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  k ~ 1,
  nl = TRUE
)
```

#### fit model
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_mod_sex <- brm(
  formula = mod_sex,
  data = dat_sex_mod,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = moult_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  seed = 123
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(list(fitted_model = fit_mod_sex, data = dat_sex_mod),
        file = here("out/sex_mod_.rds"))
```

### Analysis: Breeding Phenology model
We then retained sex in the model and tested first breeding date, last nest initiation date, and last breeding date as separate predictors of molt timing ($t_0$). Any carry-over effect of breeding should appear first in the timing of the decline, so here we focus on whether an earlier onset of breeding, later nest initiation, or later breeding activity shifts the molt midpoint. We fit the three breeding-phenology predictors singly because they describe related parts of the breeding season and the question here is whether each trait shows evidence for a carry-over association when considered in isolation.

#### datasets
Here we wrangle the full breeding phenology dataset (`dat_breeding_mod`), which is the version used in the main analysis and reported in the paper. The same complete-case dataset is used for the single-predictor breeding-phenology models so the estimates differ only in which breeding trait is entered in the $t_0$ submodel.
```{r}
# wrangle data
dat_breeding_mod <- dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season,
         last_breeding_date_J_snum,
         first_breeding_date_J_snum,
         last_nest_first_obs_J_snum) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season,
          last_breeding_date_J_snum,
          first_breeding_date_J_snum,
          last_nest_first_obs_J_snum) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
breeding_phenology_trait_lookup <- tibble::tribble(
  ~trait, ~date_col, ~description,
  "last_breeding_date_J_snum", "last_date_breeding_final",
  "Last breeding date",
  "first_breeding_date_J_snum", "first_date_breeding_final",
  "First breeding date",
  "last_nest_first_obs_J_snum", "last_nest_first_obs",
  "Last nest first observed"
)

as_breeding_date <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "Date")) {
    x
  } else {
    as.Date(x, origin = "1970-01-01")
  }
}

format_day_month <- function(x) {
  format(x, "%d %b")
}

format_season_day <- function(x) {
  ref_date <- as.Date("2001-07-01")

  if (dplyr::near(x, round(x))) {
    format_day_month(ref_date + round(x) - 1)
  } else {
    paste(
      format_day_month(ref_date + floor(x) - 1),
      format_day_month(ref_date + ceiling(x) - 1),
      sep = " / "
    )
  }
}

dat_breeding_trait_dates <- dat_breeding %>%
  semi_join(
    dat_breeding_mod %>%
      distinct(rings_comb, season),
    by = c("rings_comb", "season")
  ) %>%
  select(
    rings_comb,
    season,
    all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$date_col),
    all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$trait)
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  drop_na(all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$trait)) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$date_col),
      as_breeding_date
    )
  )

breeding_phenology_summary_stats <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  breeding_phenology_trait_lookup,
  function(trait, date_col, description) {
    trait_dates <- dat_breeding_trait_dates %>%
      transmute(
        breeding_date = .data[[date_col]],
        season_day = as.integer(
          breeding_date - as.Date(paste0(as.character(season), "-07-01"))
        ) + 1
      )

    min_i <- which.min(trait_dates$season_day)
    max_i <- which.max(trait_dates$season_day)
    min_day <- trait_dates$season_day[[min_i]]
    max_day <- trait_dates$season_day[[max_i]]

    tibble(
      Trait = trait,
      Description = description,
      `n bird-seasons` = nrow(trait_dates),
      Range = paste(
        format_day_month(trait_dates$breeding_date[[min_i]]),
        format_day_month(trait_dates$breeding_date[[max_i]]),
        sep = " - "
      ),
      `Span (days)` = max_day - min_day,
      Median = format_season_day(median(trait_dates$season_day))
    )
  }
)
```

The complete-case breeding phenology dataset contained `r nrow(dat_breeding_mod)` photo observations from `r n_distinct(dat_breeding_mod$rings_comb)` individuals and `r nrow(dat_breeding_trait_dates)` bird-seasons. Because the same breeding date is repeated across photos within a bird-season, the descriptive summary below is calculated once per bird-season. Dates are reported as day-month values on the July-to-June breeding-season calendar, and the span is the difference in days between the maximum and minimum dates.

```{r, echo=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  breeding_phenology_summary_stats,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "l", "r", "l")
)
```

#### model formula specification
```{r}
mod_sex_first_breed_only <- bf(
  score ~ 1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0)))),
  baseline ~ sex + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  t0 ~ sex + season + first_breeding_date_J_snum + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),

mod_sex_last_breed_only <- bf(

mod_sex_last_nest_first_obs_only <- bf(
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_mod_sex_last_nest_first_obs_only <- brm(
```

### Analysis: Age Class model
We next incorporated age class (first-year versus after-first-year) to the sex-specific model to test on a subser of known aged birds whether individuals in the first molt cycle differ from after-first-year birds in baseline plumage and molt timing.

#### dataset
```{r}
# wrangle data
dat_age_class_mod <- dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season, age_class) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season, age_class) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame()
```

#### model formula specification
```{r}
mod_sex_age_class <- bf(
  score ~ 1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0)))),
  baseline ~ sex + age_class + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  t0 ~ sex + season + age_class + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  k ~ 1,
  nl = TRUE
)
```

#### fit model
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_mod_sex_age_class <- brm(
  formula = mod_sex_age_class,
  data = dat_age_class_mod,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = moult_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  seed = 123
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(list(fitted_model = fit_mod_sex_age_class,
             data = dat_age_class_mod),
        file = here("out/sex_age_class_mod_2.rds"))
```

### Analysis: Continuous Age model
Following Van de Pol & Verhulst (2006), we decomposed age ($x_{ist}$) into each bird's mean age across the three-year study period ($\bar{x}_i$; the between-individual effect, implemented as `avg_age`) and the deviation from that mean for a given observation ($x_{ist} - \bar{x}_i$; the within-individual effect, implemented as `age_dev`). Because the age-class model already tests the first-year versus after-first-year contrast directly, we fit the continuous-age model only to after-first-year (AFY) observations (`age > 1`) to ask whether any age effect persists beyond that initial transition.

#### datasets
Here we use an AFY-only continuous age dataset (`dat_age_mod`), excluding age-1 observations so that the within- and between-individual age terms quantify age-related variation among older birds only.
```{r}
# calculate average age in the AFY-only dataset of individuals of known age
avg_ages <-
  dat_breeding %>%
  distinct(rings_comb, age) %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  filter(age > 1) %>%
  group_by(rings_comb) %>%
  summarise(avg_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))

# wrangle data
dat_age_mod <- dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season, age) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  # center age
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  filter(age > 1) %>%
  left_join(., avg_ages, by = "rings_comb") %>%
  # age deviance
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(age_dev = age - avg_age) %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb,
          season, avg_age, age_dev) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame()
```

#### model formula specification
```{r}
mod_sex_age_avg <- bf(
  score ~ 1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0)))),
  baseline ~ sex + age_dev + avg_age + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  t0 ~ sex + season + age_dev + avg_age + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  k ~ 1,
  nl = TRUE
)
```

#### fit model
We fit the main continuous-age model to the AFY-only known-age dataset here.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_mod_sex_age_avg <- brm(
  formula = mod_sex_age_avg,
  data = dat_age_mod,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = moult_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  seed = 123
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(list(fitted_model = fit_mod_sex_age_avg,
             data = dat_age_mod),
        file = here("out/sex_age_avg_mod_.rds"))
```

### Analysis: Migratory Strategy model
We finally tested whether migratory strategy explained variation in
$\beta$ and $t_0$ after accounting for sex. If migration imposes tighter
late-season constraints, we would expect migrants to move through the
post-breeding transition earlier than residents.

#### datasets
```{r}
# wrangle data
dat_migratory_status_mod <-
  dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season, migratory_status) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season, migratory_status) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame()
```

#### model formula specification
```{r}
mod_sex_migratory_status <- bf(
  score ~ 1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0)))),
  baseline ~ sex + migratory_status + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  t0 ~ sex + season + migratory_status + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  k ~ 1,
  nl = TRUE
)
```

#### fit model
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_mod_sex_migratory_status <- brm(
  formula = mod_sex_migratory_status,
  data = dat_migratory_status_mod,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = moult_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  seed = 123
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(list(fitted_model = fit_mod_sex_migratory_status,
             data = dat_migratory_status_mod),
        file = here("out/sex_migratory_status_mod_.rds"))
```

## Results
Using 1,646 scored photographs from 100 birds across three seasons, we found that 1) baseline rufous band score showed clear persistent differences among birds, whereas evidence for cross-year repeatability in molt timing was weak, 2) age explained variation primarily through the first-year versus after-first-year contrast, with little evidence for additional continuous age trends among AFY birds, and 3) the single-predictor breeding-phenology models showed clear positive associations between later last nest initiation, later last breeding date, and molt midpoint, while first breeding date showed little evidence of an association. Migratory strategy did not clearly shift the molt schedule. The results below start from the saved model objects in `out/`, so this section can be rerun without refitting the time-consuming Bayesian models above. Helper chunks are hidden in the HTML to keep the shared document readable, while the visible chunks show only the short code needed to reproduce the reported tables.

```{r results-helpers, include=FALSE}
# Summarise posterior draws as a median and 95% credible interval.
summarise_posterior <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    ci_lower = as.numeric(quantile(x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)),
    ci_upper = as.numeric(quantile(x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
}

# Format numeric intervals consistently across all reported tables.
format_numeric_interval <- function(summary_tbl, digits = 2) {
  paste0(
    round(summary_tbl$median, digits), " [",
    round(summary_tbl$ci_lower, digits), ", ",
    round(summary_tbl$ci_upper, digits), "]"
  )
}

# Convert shifted Julian dates back to the month-day labels used in the text tables.
shifted_julian_to_date <- function(x, origin_year = 2021) {
  as.Date(x - 182, origin = paste0(origin_year, "-01-01"))
}

format_shifted_julian_interval <- function(summary_tbl, digits = 2, origin_year = 2021) {
  paste0(
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(summary_tbl$median, origin_year), "%d %b")), " [",
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(summary_tbl$ci_lower, origin_year), "%d %b")), ", ",
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(summary_tbl$ci_upper, origin_year), "%d %b")), "]"
  )
}

# Build a summary row once the estimate has been reduced to a point estimate and interval.
summary_row_from_stats <- function(parameter, type, parameter_group, stats,
                                   digits = 2,
                                   formatter = format_numeric_interval, ...) {
  tibble(
    type = type,
    parameter_ = parameter_group,
    parameter = parameter,
    estimate = stats$median,
    ci_lower = stats$ci_lower,
    ci_upper = stats$ci_upper,
    median_CI = formatter(stats, digits = digits, ...)
  )
}

# Convenience wrapper when we start from raw posterior draws.
summary_row <- function(parameter, type, parameter_group, draws,
                        digits = 2,
                        formatter = format_numeric_interval, ...) {
  summary_row_from_stats(
    parameter = parameter,
    type = type,
    parameter_group = parameter_group,
    stats = summarise_posterior(draws),
    digits = digits,
    formatter = formatter,
    ...
  )
}

# Recover the season-weighted centering/scaling constants used to back-transform t0.
weighted_date_scaling <- function(data, date_col = "date_J") {
  if (all(c("date_J_mean_ref", "date_J_sd_ref") %in% names(data))) {
    date_stats <- data %>%
      group_by(season) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_value = first(date_J_mean_ref),
        sd_value = first(date_J_sd_ref),
        n = dplyr::n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  } else {
    date_stats <- data %>%
      group_by(season) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_value = mean(.data[[date_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_value = sd(.data[[date_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
        n = dplyr::n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  }

  tibble(
    weighted_mean = weighted.mean(date_stats$mean_value, w = date_stats$n, na.rm = TRUE),
    weighted_sd = weighted.mean(date_stats$sd_value, w = date_stats$n, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# Summarise breeding-phenology effects using directional contrasts:
# advances for first breeding date and delays for later breeding dates.
breeding_predictor_specs <- tibble(
  predictor = c(
    "first_breeding_date_J_snum",
    "last_nest_first_obs_J_snum",
    "last_breeding_date_J_snum"
  ),
  display_label = c(
    "First breeding date",
    "Last nest initiation date",
    "Last breeding date"
  ),
  row_label = c(
    "Δ pre-basic moult midpoint (t0; days) per 1-day advance in first breeding date",
    "Δ pre-basic moult midpoint (t0; days) per 1-day delay in last nest initiation date",
    "Δ pre-basic moult midpoint (t0; days) per 1-day delay in last breeding date"
  ),
  multiplier = c(-1, 1, 1)
)

extract_breeding_effect_draws <- function(model_obj, predictor) {
  breed_post <- as_draws_df(model_obj$fitted_model)
  date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(model_obj$data)
  predictor_spec <- breeding_predictor_specs %>%
    filter(.data$predictor == .env$predictor)

  if (nrow(predictor_spec) != 1) {
    stop("Unknown breeding predictor: ", predictor)
  }

  effect_col <- paste0("b_t0_", predictor)

  if (!effect_col %in% names(breed_post)) {
    stop("Predictor ", predictor, " not found in fitted model.")
  }

  breed_post[[effect_col]] * date_scale$weighted_sd * predictor_spec$multiplier[[1]]
}

summarise_breeding_effect <- function(model_obj, predictor) {
  predictor_spec <- breeding_predictor_specs %>%
    filter(.data$predictor == .env$predictor)

  summary_row(
    predictor_spec$row_label[[1]],
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Breeding phenology",
    extract_breeding_effect_draws(model_obj, predictor)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      predictor = predictor_spec$predictor[[1]],
      predictor_label = predictor_spec$display_label[[1]]
    )
}

summarise_breeding_effects <- function(model_obj) {
  bind_rows(lapply(
    breeding_predictor_specs$predictor,
    function(predictor_i) summarise_breeding_effect(model_obj, predictor_i)
  ))
}

summarise_single_breeding_effects <- function(single_model_list) {
  bind_rows(lapply(
    seq_len(nrow(breeding_predictor_specs)),
    function(i) {
      predictor_i <- breeding_predictor_specs$predictor[[i]]
      summarise_breeding_effect(single_model_list[[predictor_i]], predictor_i)
    }
  ))
}

find_posterior_draw_col <- function(post, patterns, description) {
  col_name <- names(post)[Reduce(`&`, lapply(patterns, grepl, x = names(post)))]

  if (length(col_name) != 1) {
    stop("Could not identify posterior draw column for ", description, ".")
  }

  col_name
}

find_posterior_draw_col_by_terms <- function(post, include_terms, description,
                                             exclude_terms = character()) {
  col_names <- names(post)[grepl("^b_t0_", names(post))]
  keep_include <- Reduce(
    `&`,
    lapply(include_terms, function(term) grepl(term, col_names, fixed = TRUE))
  )

  if (length(exclude_terms) > 0) {
    keep_exclude <- Reduce(
      `|`,
      lapply(exclude_terms, function(term) grepl(term, col_names, fixed = TRUE))
    )
  } else {
    keep_exclude <- rep(FALSE, length(col_names))
  }

  col_name <- col_names[keep_include & !keep_exclude]

  if (length(col_name) != 1) {
    stop("Could not identify posterior draw column for ", description, ".")
  }

  col_name
}

summarise_parental_state_last_breeding_effect <- function(model_obj) {
  post <- as_draws_df(model_obj$fitted_model)
  date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(model_obj$data)
  last_breeding_col <- "b_t0_last_breeding_date_J_snum"
  parental_state_col <- "b_t0_parental_statebrood"
  interaction_col <- find_posterior_draw_col(
    post,
    c("^b_t0_", "last_breeding_date_J_snum", "parental_statebrood", ":"),
    "last breeding date by parental state interaction"
  )

  nest_slope <- post[[last_breeding_col]] * date_scale$weighted_sd
  brood_slope <- (post[[last_breeding_col]] + post[[interaction_col]]) * date_scale$weighted_sd
  brood_minus_nest_slope <- post[[interaction_col]] * date_scale$weighted_sd
  brood_minus_nest_midpoint <- post[[parental_state_col]] * date_scale$weighted_sd

  bind_rows(
    summary_row(
      "Δ pre-basic moult midpoint (t0; days) per 1-day delay in last breeding date, incubation/nest",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Breeding phenology by parental state",
      nest_slope
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Δ pre-basic moult midpoint (t0; days) per 1-day delay in last breeding date, brood care",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Breeding phenology by parental state",
      brood_slope
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Difference in last-breeding-date effect (brood care − incubation/nest; days per day)",
      "Posterior contrasts",
      "Breeding phenology by parental state",
      brood_minus_nest_slope
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Parental-state effect at mean last breeding date (brood care − incubation/nest; days)",
      "Posterior contrasts",
      "Breeding phenology by parental state",
      brood_minus_nest_midpoint
    )
  )
}

summarise_sex_parental_state_last_breeding_effect <- function(model_obj) {
  post <- as_draws_df(model_obj$fitted_model)
  date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(model_obj$data)
  last_breeding_col <- "b_t0_last_breeding_date_J_snum"
  last_breeding_state_col <- find_posterior_draw_col_by_terms(
    post,
    include_terms = c("last_breeding_date_J_snum", "parental_statebrood"),
    exclude_terms = "sexM",
    description = "last breeding date by parental state interaction"
  )
  last_breeding_sex_col <- find_posterior_draw_col_by_terms(
    post,
    include_terms = c("last_breeding_date_J_snum", "sexM"),
    exclude_terms = "parental_statebrood",
    description = "last breeding date by sex interaction"
  )
  last_breeding_state_sex_col <- find_posterior_draw_col_by_terms(
    post,
    include_terms = c("last_breeding_date_J_snum", "parental_statebrood", "sexM"),
    description = "last breeding date by parental state by sex interaction"
  )

  female_nest_slope <- post[[last_breeding_col]] * date_scale$weighted_sd
  female_brood_slope <- (
    post[[last_breeding_col]] +
      post[[last_breeding_state_col]]
  ) * date_scale$weighted_sd
  male_nest_slope <- (
    post[[last_breeding_col]] +
      post[[last_breeding_sex_col]]
  ) * date_scale$weighted_sd
  male_brood_slope <- (
    post[[last_breeding_col]] +
      post[[last_breeding_state_col]] +
      post[[last_breeding_sex_col]] +
      post[[last_breeding_state_sex_col]]
  ) * date_scale$weighted_sd

  female_minus_male_nest <- female_nest_slope - male_nest_slope
  female_minus_male_brood <- female_brood_slope - male_brood_slope
  brood_minus_nest_sex_difference <- female_minus_male_brood - female_minus_male_nest

  bind_rows(
    summary_row(
      "Female slope: incubation/nest",
      "Posterior estimates (sex- and state-specific slopes)",
      "Sex by parental state",
      female_nest_slope
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Male slope: incubation/nest",
      "Posterior estimates (sex- and state-specific slopes)",
      "Sex by parental state",
      male_nest_slope
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Female slope: brood care",
      "Posterior estimates (sex- and state-specific slopes)",
      "Sex by parental state",
      female_brood_slope
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Male slope: brood care",
      "Posterior estimates (sex- and state-specific slopes)",
      "Sex by parental state",
      male_brood_slope
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Female - male slope difference: incubation/nest",
      "Posterior contrasts",
      "Sex by parental state",
      female_minus_male_nest
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Female - male slope difference: brood care",
      "Posterior contrasts",
      "Sex by parental state",
      female_minus_male_brood
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Change in female - male slope difference: brood care - incubation/nest",
      "Posterior contrasts",
      "Sex by parental state",
      brood_minus_nest_sex_difference
    )
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      pr_positive = c(
        mean(female_nest_slope > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean(male_nest_slope > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean(female_brood_slope > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean(male_brood_slope > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean(female_minus_male_nest > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean(female_minus_male_brood > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean(brood_minus_nest_sex_difference > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
      )
    )
}

previous_single_breeding_effect_summary <- function() {
  stats <- tibble(
    predictor = c(
      "first_breeding_date_J_snum",
      "last_nest_first_obs_J_snum",
      "last_breeding_date_J_snum"
    ),
    estimate = c(0.01, 0.21, 0.17),
    ci_lower = c(-0.16, 0.05, 0.04),
    ci_upper = c(0.18, 0.37, 0.31)
  )

  breeding_predictor_specs %>%
    left_join(stats, by = "predictor") %>%
    mutate(
      type = "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      parameter_ = "Breeding phenology",
      parameter = row_label,
      median_CI = format_numeric_interval(
        tibble(
          median = estimate,
          ci_lower = ci_lower,
          ci_upper = ci_upper
        )
      ),
      predictor_label = display_label
    ) %>%
    select(type, parameter_, parameter, estimate, ci_lower, ci_upper,
           median_CI, predictor, predictor_label)
}

# Convert `performance::r2_bayes()` output into the same table-ready format used elsewhere.
summarise_bayes_r2 <- function(fitted_model) {
  r2_df <- performance::r2_bayes(fitted_model) %>% as.data.frame()

  tibble(
    parameter = c("Marginal R²", "Conditional R²"),
    median = c(r2_df$R2[2], r2_df$R2[1]),
    ci_lower = c(r2_df$CI_low[2], r2_df$CI_low[1]),
    ci_upper = c(r2_df$CI_high[2], r2_df$CI_high[1])
  )
}

# Add repeatability- and variance-related draws used in the sex-only summary table.
add_repeatability_draws <- function(post) {
  post %>%
    mutate(
      var_baseline_rings_comb = sd_rings_comb__baseline_Intercept^2,
      var_t0_rings_comb = sd_rings_comb__t0_Intercept^2,
      var_baseline_rings_comb_season =
        `sd_rings_comb:season__baseline_Intercept`^2,
      var_t0_rings_comb_season =
        `sd_rings_comb:season__t0_Intercept`^2,
      var_baseline_total =
        var_baseline_rings_comb + var_baseline_rings_comb_season + sigma^2,
      var_t0_total =
        var_t0_rings_comb + var_t0_rings_comb_season + sigma^2,
      # Across-year repeatability is the correlation between repeated measures
      # from the same bird in different seasons, so only the bird-level effect
      # contributes to the shared variance.
      R_baseline_between_year = var_baseline_rings_comb / var_baseline_total,
      R_t0_between_year = var_t0_rings_comb / var_t0_total,
      # Within-year repeatability is the correlation between repeated measures
      # from the same bird in the same season, so both bird- and bird-season-
      # level effects contribute to the shared variance.
      R_baseline_within_year =
        (var_baseline_rings_comb + var_baseline_rings_comb_season) / var_baseline_total,
      R_t0_within_year =
        (var_t0_rings_comb + var_t0_rings_comb_season) / var_t0_total,
      cor_baseline_t0 = cor_rings_comb__baseline_Intercept__t0_Intercept,
      resid_var = sigma^2
    )
}

get_model_season_levels <- function(model_obj) {
  if (!"season" %in% names(model_obj$data)) {
    return(character())
  }

  if (is.factor(model_obj$data$season)) {
    levels(droplevels(model_obj$data$season))
  } else {
    sort(unique(as.character(model_obj$data$season)))
  }
}

has_t0_season_effect <- function(post) {
  any(grepl("^b_t0_season", names(post)))
}

extract_t0_season_draws <- function(model_obj, post = NULL) {
  if (is.null(post)) {
    post <- as_draws_df(model_obj$fitted_model)
  }

  season_levels <- get_model_season_levels(model_obj)

  if (length(season_levels) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }

  season_stats <- model_obj$data %>%
    select(any_of(c("season", "date_J_mean_ref", "date_J_sd_ref"))) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(season = as.character(season))

  if (!all(c("date_J_mean_ref", "date_J_sd_ref") %in% names(season_stats))) {
    season_stats <- date_scaling_ref %>%
      filter(season %in% season_levels) %>%
      mutate(season = as.character(season))
  }

  setNames(lapply(season_levels, function(season_i) {
    season_coef_name <- paste0("b_t0_season", season_i)
    season_draws <- post$b_t0_Intercept

    if (season_coef_name %in% names(post)) {
      season_draws <- season_draws + post[[season_coef_name]]
    }

    season_ref <- season_stats %>%
      filter(season == season_i)

    season_draws * season_ref$date_J_sd_ref + season_ref$date_J_mean_ref
  }), season_levels)
}

season_t0_parameter_names <- function(model_obj) {
  season_levels <- get_model_season_levels(model_obj)

  if (length(season_levels) < 2) {
    return(character())
  }

  c(
    paste0(
      "Pre-basic moult midpoint (t0), season ",
      season_levels,
      ", females (reference)"
    ),
    vapply(combn(season_levels, 2, simplify = FALSE), function(season_pair) {
      paste0(
        "Season effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): ",
        season_pair[[2]],
        " - ",
        season_pair[[1]]
      )
    }, character(1))
  )
}

summarise_t0_season_effects <- function(
    model_obj,
    type = "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    parameter_group = "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)") {
  post <- as_draws_df(model_obj$fitted_model)

  if (!has_t0_season_effect(post)) {
    return(tibble())
  }

  season_draws <- extract_t0_season_draws(model_obj, post)
  season_levels <- names(season_draws)
  season_pairs <- combn(season_levels, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  bind_rows(
    bind_rows(lapply(season_levels, function(season_i) {
      summary_row(
        paste0(
          "Pre-basic moult midpoint (t0), season ",
          season_i,
          ", females (reference)"
        ),
        type,
        parameter_group,
        season_draws[[season_i]],
        formatter = format_shifted_julian_interval
      )
    })),
    bind_rows(lapply(season_pairs, function(season_pair) {
      summary_row(
        paste0(
          "Season effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): ",
          season_pair[[2]],
          " - ",
          season_pair[[1]]
        ),
        type,
        parameter_group,
        season_draws[[season_pair[[2]]]] - season_draws[[season_pair[[1]]]]
      )
    }))
  )
}

pick_parameter_rows <- function(tbl, parameters) {
  tbl %>%
    mutate(.order = match(parameter, parameters)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.order)) %>%
    arrange(.order) %>%
    select(-.order)
}

# Keep the HTML diagnostics compact by reducing each fitted model to a few convergence checks.
model_diagnostics_table <- function(model_list) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(model_list, function(model_obj, model_name) {
    draw_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(
      posterior::as_draws_array(model_obj$fitted_model),
      "rhat",
      "ess_bulk",
      "ess_tail"
    )

    tibble(
      model = model_name,
      max_rhat = round(max(draw_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      n_rhat_over_1_01 = sum(draw_summary$rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_bulk_ess = floor(min(draw_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE)),
      min_tail_ess = floor(min(draw_summary$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE))
    )
  })
}

# Use the same simple table style across the Results section.
display_result_table <- function(tbl) {
  tbl %>%
    select(parameter, median_CI) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      parameter = "Parameter",
      median_CI = gt::md("Posterior median [95% CrI]")
    ) %>%
    cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything())
}

display_consolidated_table <- function(tbl) {
  count_model_individuals <- function(obj_name, fallback) {
    if (exists(obj_name, inherits = TRUE)) {
      obj <- get(obj_name, inherits = TRUE)
      if (is.list(obj) && "data" %in% names(obj) && "rings_comb" %in% names(obj$data)) {
        return(dplyr::n_distinct(obj$data$rings_comb))
      }
    }

    fallback
  }

  format_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
    out <- format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
    out <- sub("(?<=\\d)0+$", "", out, perl = TRUE)
    out <- sub("\\.$", "", out)
    out <- sub("^-0$", "0", out)
    out
  }

  format_date_median <- function(x, origin_year = 2021) {
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(x, origin_year), "%d %b"))
  }

  format_date_ci <- function(lo, hi, origin_year = 2021) {
    paste0(
      "[",
      sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(lo, origin_year), "%d %b")),
      ", ",
      sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(hi, origin_year), "%d %b")),
      "]"
    )
  }

  n_lookup <- c(
    "Sex-specific" = count_model_individuals("sex_mod", 100L),
    "Breeding phenology" = count_model_individuals("sex_last_breed_only_mod", 81L),
    "Age-class" = count_model_individuals("sex_age_class_mod", 86L),
    "Continuous age (AFY only)" = count_model_individuals("sex_age_avg_mod", 22L),
    "Migratory status" = count_model_individuals("sex_migratory_status_mod", 41L)
  )

  section_levels <- c(
    "Fixed effects on baseline breeding plumage score (β)",
    "Fixed effects on post-breeding molt midpoint (t0): season, sex, age-class, and migration strategy",
    "Fixed effects on post-breeding molt midpoint (t0): effect of 1-day change in breeding phenology trait",
    "Derived fixed effects: post-breeding molt rate at t0",
    "Repeatability of molt traits (R)",
    "Model fit",
    "Variance components and residual structure"
  )

  display_tbl <- tbl %>%
    mutate(
      section = case_when(
        grepl(
          "first breeding date|last nest initiation date|last breeding date",
          parameter,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~
          "Fixed effects on post-breeding molt midpoint (t0): effect of 1-day change in breeding phenology trait",
        grepl("rate at inflection", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Derived fixed effects: post-breeding molt rate at t0",
        type == "Repeatability" ~ "Repeatability of molt traits (R)",
        type == "Model-level goodness-of-fit" ~ "Model fit",
        type %in% c(
          "Between-individual variance (random effects)",
          "Random-effects correlation",
          "Residual (within-observation) variance"
        ) ~ "Variance components and residual structure",
        grepl("baseline alternate plumage score", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Fixed effects on baseline breeding plumage score (β)",
        grepl("moult mid", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Fixed effects on post-breeding molt midpoint (t0): season, sex, age-class, and migration strategy",
        TRUE ~ type
      ),
      row_label = case_when(
        grepl("^Baseline alternate plumage score.*females", parameter) ~
          "Intercept, females (reference; score)",
        grepl("^Sex effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Sex effect (males – females; Δ score)",
        grepl("^Age-class effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Age-class effect (AFY – FY; Δ score)",
        grepl("^Between-individual age effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Between-individual age effect (Δ score)",
        grepl("^Within-individual age effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Within-individual age effect (Δ score)",
        grepl("^Migratory-strategy effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Migratory-strategy effect (Resident – Migrant; Δ score)",
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint \\(t0\\), season", parameter) ~
          paste0(
            "Season ",
            stringr::str_extract(parameter, "\\d{4}"),
            " midpoint, females (reference; date)"
          ),
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint.*females", parameter) ~
          "Intercept, females (reference; date)",
        grepl("^Season effect on pre-basic moult midpoint", parameter) ~
          paste0(
            "Season effect (",
            stringr::str_match(parameter, "t0\\): (.*)$")[, 2],
            "; Δ days)"
          ),
        grepl("^Sex effect on pre-basic moult mid", parameter) ~
          "Sex effect (males – females; Δ days)",
        grepl("^Age-class effect on pre-basic moult", parameter) ~
          "Age-class effect (AFY – FY; Δ days)",
        grepl("^Between-individual age effect on pre-basic moult midpoint", parameter) ~
          "Between-individual age effect (Δ days)",
        grepl("^Within-individual age effect on pre-basic moult midpoint", parameter) ~
          "Within-individual age effect (Δ days)",
        grepl("^Migratory-strategy effect on pre-basic moult midpoint", parameter) ~
          "Migratory-strategy effect (Resident – Migrant; Δ days)",
        grepl("first breeding date", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "First date observed breeding (Δ days per 1-day advance)",
        grepl("last nest initiation date", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Last nest initiation date (Δ days per 1-day delay)",
        grepl("last breeding date", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Last date observed breeding (Δ days per 1-day delay)",
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult rate at inflection.*females", parameter) ~
          "Intercept, females (reference; days·score⁻¹)",
        grepl("^Sex effect on pre-basic moult rate at inflection", parameter) ~
          "Sex effect (males – females; days·score⁻¹)",
        parameter == "Between-year repeatability of alternate plumage" ~
          "Between-year repeatability of β",
        parameter == "Within-year repeatability of alternate plumage" ~
          "Within-year repeatability of β",
        parameter == "Between-year repeatability of pre-basic moult mid-point date" ~
          "Between-year repeatability of t0",
        parameter == "Within-year repeatability of pre-basic moult mid-point date" ~
          "Within-year repeatability of t0",
        parameter == "Between-individual variance in baseline plumage score" ~
          "Between-individual variance in β",
        parameter == "Between-individual variance in pre-basic moult midpoint date" ~
          "Between-individual variance in t0",
        grepl("^Correlation between baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Correlation between β and t0",
        TRUE ~ parameter
      ),
      model = case_when(
        grepl("^Age-class effect", parameter) ~ "Age-class",
        grepl("^Between-individual age effect|^Within-individual age effect", parameter) ~
          "Continuous age (AFY only)",
        grepl("^Migratory-strategy effect", parameter) ~ "Migratory status",
        grepl(
          "first breeding date|last nest initiation date|last breeding date",
          parameter,
          ignore.case = TRUE
        ) ~
          "Breeding phenology",
        TRUE ~ "Sex-specific"
      ),
      n_ind = as.integer(unname(n_lookup[model])),
      posterior_median = if_else(
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint.*females", parameter),
        format_date_median(estimate),
        format_num(estimate)
      ),
      credible_interval = if_else(
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint.*females", parameter),
        format_date_ci(ci_lower, ci_upper),
        paste0("[", format_num(ci_lower), ", ", format_num(ci_upper), "]")
      ),
      section = factor(section, levels = section_levels)
    ) %>%
    select(section, row_label, posterior_median, credible_interval, n_ind, model)

  display_tbl %>%
    gt::gt(groupname_col = "section", rowname_col = "row_label") %>%
    gt::tab_stubhead(label = "") %>%
    gt::cols_label(
      posterior_median = "Posterior median",
      credible_interval = "[95% CrI]",
      n_ind = gt::html("N<sub>ind</sub>"),
      model = "Model"
    ) %>%
    gt::cols_align(
      align = "center",
      columns = c(posterior_median, credible_interval, n_ind)
    ) %>%
    gt::cols_align(align = "left", columns = model) %>%
    gt::cols_width(
      gt::stub() ~ gt::px(360),
      posterior_median ~ gt::px(115),
      credible_interval ~ gt::px(150),
      n_ind ~ gt::px(60),
      model ~ gt::px(150)
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = gt::cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_borders(sides = "top", color = "black", weight = gt::px(1)),
      locations = gt::cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width = gt::pct(100),
      table.font.size = gt::px(12),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(3),
      row_group.padding = gt::px(4),
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(11)
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_source_note(
      source_note = gt::md(
        "Note: Δ denotes an additive difference relative to the reference category (for categorical predictors) or the expected change in the response per unit change in the predictor (for continuous covariates)."
      )
    )
}
```

### Results: Sex-specific model
We use the sex model as the main reference because it uses the full dataset. It shows clear sex differences in baseline ornament expression, clear season-to-season shifts in molt midpoint, little evidence for a sex difference in midpoint, and strong repeatability in baseline ornament expression but limited between-year repeatability in timing.

```{r results-sex-model, echo=FALSE}
# Start from the saved posterior draws so this chunk reproduces the reported table without refitting.
sex_post <- as_draws_df(sex_mod$fitted_model)

# Use season-weighted centering/scaling constants to convert the model's t0 estimate back to days.
date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(sex_mod$data)
mean_date_sd <- date_scale$weighted_sd
mean_date_mean <- date_scale$weighted_mean

# Derive the biological quantities reported in the consolidated table.
sex_post <- sex_post %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_sexF = b_baseline_Intercept,
    baseline_sexM = b_baseline_Intercept + b_baseline_sexM,
    baseline_sex_diff = b_baseline_sexM,
    t0_sexF = b_t0_Intercept * mean_date_sd + mean_date_mean,
    t0_sex_diff = b_t0_sexM * mean_date_sd,
    rate_days_score_sexF = 1 / (((baseline_sexF - 1) * b_k_Intercept) / (4 * mean_date_sd)),
    rate_days_score_sexM = 1 / (((baseline_sexM - 1) * b_k_Intercept) / (4 * mean_date_sd)),
    rate_days_score_diff = rate_days_score_sexM - rate_days_score_sexF
  ) %>%
  add_repeatability_draws()

# Bayesian R² is already summarised, so convert it directly into table rows.
sex_r2 <- summarise_bayes_r2(sex_mod$fitted_model)
sex_t0_rows <- if (has_t0_season_effect(sex_post)) {
  bind_rows(
    summarise_t0_season_effects(sex_mod),
    summary_row(
      "Sex effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): males − females",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
      sex_post$t0_sex_diff
    )
  )
} else {
  bind_rows(
    summary_row(
      "Pre-basic moult midpoint (t0), females (reference)",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
      sex_post$t0_sexF,
      formatter = format_shifted_julian_interval
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Sex effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): males − females",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
      sex_post$t0_sex_diff
    )
  )
}

sex_mod_summary_table <- bind_rows(
  summary_row(
    "Baseline alternate plumage score (β), females (reference)",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Full alternate plumage score (beta)",
    sex_post$baseline_sexF
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Sex effect on baseline alternate plumage score (β): males − females",

  ),

  summary_row(

  ),
  summary_row(
    "Sex effect on pre-basic moult rate at inflection (days·score⁻¹): males − females",

  ),
  summary_row(
    "Between-year repeatability of alternate plumage",

  ),

  ),
```

### Results: Breeding Phenology model
When entered singly, later last nest initiation and later last breeding date showed positive associations with the post-breeding molt midpoint. In contrast, the single-predictor model for first breeding date showed little evidence for a shift in molt timing.

```{r results-breeding-phenology-model, echo=FALSE}
single_breeding_effect_summary_table <- if (!is.null(single_breeding_models)) {
  summarise_single_breeding_effects(single_breeding_models)
} else {
  previous_single_breeding_effect_summary()
}

display_result_table(single_breeding_effect_summary_table)
```

### Results: Age Class model
The age-class model showed a clear contrast between first-year and after-first-year birds, driven mainly by later molt midpoints in older birds. There was little evidence for an accompanying difference in baseline plumage score.

```{r results-age-class-model, echo=FALSE}
age_class_post <- as_draws_df(sex_age_class_mod$fitted_model)

# Convert the age-class t0 effect from scaled units back to days.
date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(sex_age_class_mod$data)
mean_date_sd <- date_scale$weighted_sd

sex_age_class_mod_summary_table <- bind_rows(
  summary_row(
    "Age-class effect on baseline alternate plumage score (β): AFY − FY",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Full alternate plumage score (beta)",
    age_class_post$b_baseline_age_classAFY
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Age-class effect on pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0): AFY − FY",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
    age_class_post$b_t0_age_classAFY * mean_date_sd
  )
)

display_result_table(sex_age_class_mod_summary_table)
```

### Results: Continuous Age model (AFY only)
Restricting the continuous-age analysis to AFY birds asked whether age continued to explain molt variation after the first-year transition. There was little clear evidence for either between- or within-individual age effects on baseline plumage score or molt midpoint among AFY birds.

### Results: Migratory Strategy model
Residents and migrants showed similar baseline plumage scores and molt timing, with broad overlap in both traits.

## Figures
The manuscript's Figure 1 is reproduced as two adjacent components in this
document: the static photo montage and scoring panel above (`Figure 1a`) and
the code-generated overview panel below (`Figure 1b`).

### Figure 1b - raw data overview

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code for figure 2"
breeding_data_all <- readRDS(here("data/breeding_KK_data.rds"))

#### breeding histograms
# 1) Get per-season centering/scaling constants from the ORIGINAL (unscaled) shifted-Julian variables
stats <- breeding_data_all %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(
    mu_last  = mean(last_breeding_date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_last  = sd(last_breeding_date_J,  na.rm = TRUE),
    mu_first = mean(first_breeding_date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_first = sd(first_breeding_date_J,  na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2) Join constants, invert transform, then convert shifted-Julian (1 = Jul 1) to a common calendar date
ref_start <- as.Date("2001-07-01")  # any non-leap year works well

out_dates <- dat_breeding %>%
  distinct(rings_comb, season,
           last_breeding_date_J_snum,
           first_breeding_date_J_snum) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  left_join(stats, by = "season") %>%
  mutate(
    # If _snum is CENTER-ONLY (scale = 0): x = centered + mean
    last_J  = last_breeding_date_J_snum  + mu_last,
    first_J = first_breeding_date_J_snum + mu_first,

    # Convert shifted-Julian to a common calendar date (same year for all seasons)
    last_date_common  = ref_start + round(last_J  - 1),
    first_date_common = ref_start + round(first_J - 1),

    # Optional: month-day labels (often what you want for plotting)
    last_md  = format(last_date_common,  "%b-%d"),
    first_md = format(first_date_common, "%b-%d")
  ) %>%
  select(rings_comb, season,
         last_J, first_J,
         last_date_common, first_date_common,
         last_md, first_md)

out_dates_long <- out_dates %>%
  select(rings_comb, season, last_date_common, first_date_common) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(last_date_common, first_date_common),
    names_to = "phenology_trait",
    values_to = "date_common"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    phenology_trait = sub("_date_common$", "_date", phenology_trait),
    phenology_trait = sub("_common$", "", phenology_trait)
  )

# over lapping histograms
nesting_hist <-
  ggplot(
      out_dates_long %>%
        filter(phenology_trait %in% c("first_date", "last_date")),
      aes(x = date_common, fill = phenology_trait)
    ) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 7, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55, colour = NA) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.margin = margin(0.2, 0.2, -15, 0.2)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "left", breaks = c(0, 10, 20), limits = c(0, 25)) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_labels = "%B", expand = c(0.01, 0.01),
    date_breaks = "2 month",
    limits = c(as.Date("2001-07-01"), as.Date("2002-05-01"))

#### raw data and example individual trajectories
nests_data <- readRDS(here("data/nests_KK_data.rds"))

dates_for_plot <-
  data.frame(date_ = as.Date(c(as.Date("2021-07-01"):as.Date("2022-06-30"))),
             date_J = c(1:365))

# 1) Build a clean prediction grid for the two individuals across dates and seasons
newdata_ind <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  date_J_scaled = seq(
    from = min(sex_mod$data$date_J_scaled),
    to   = max(sex_mod$data$date_J_scaled),
    length.out = max(sex_mod$data$date_J) - min(sex_mod$data$date_J) + 1
  ),
  rings_comb = c("RRGO", "RGGL"),
  season     = levels(sex_mod$data$season)   # e.g., c("2021","2022","2023")
) %>%
  # assign sex per individual from your observed data (safer than expanding sex)
  left_join(
    sex_mod$data %>%
      distinct(rings_comb, sex) %>%
      filter(rings_comb %in% c("RRGO", "RGGL")),
    by = "rings_comb"
  ) %>%
  # if you want Julian date (unscaled) + calendar date for plotting, join your helper tables
  left_join(
    data.frame(
      date_J = seq(min(sex_mod$data$date_J), max(sex_mod$data$date_J), length.out =
                     max(sex_mod$data$date_J) - min(sex_mod$data$date_J) + 1),
      date_J_scaled = seq(min(sex_mod$data$date_J_scaled), max(sex_mod$data$date_J_scaled), length.out =
                            max(sex_mod$data$date_J) - min(sex_mod$data$date_J) + 1)
    ),
    by = "date_J_scaled"
  ) %>%
  left_join(dates_for_plot, by = "date_J")

# 2) Extract expected-value draws (includes group-level effects by default)
epred_draws_ind <- add_epred_draws(
```

### Figure 3 - state-dependent molt trajectories
This figure reproduces the manuscript's state-dependent summary of the sex,
age-class, and migratory-strategy models. The left column shows population-level
predicted molt trajectories, while the middle and right columns show the
state-specific posteriors for molt midpoint (`t0`) and the baseline rufous-band
score (`β`).

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code for Figure 3"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-dpi: 300
#| out-width: "8in"
combined_origin <- as.Date("2021-07-01")
combined_curve_limits <- c(as.Date("2021-07-20"), as.Date("2022-05-04"))
combined_curve_breaks <- seq(
  from = as.Date("2021-07-27"),
  to = as.Date("2022-04-12"),
  by = "4 weeks"
)
combined_t0_limits <- c(160, 250)
combined_t0_breaks <- seq(174, 300, by = 21)
combined_t0_visible_breaks <- combined_t0_breaks[
  combined_t0_breaks >= combined_t0_limits[1] &
    combined_t0_breaks <= combined_t0_limits[2]
]
combined_baseline_breaks <- 4:7
combined_baseline_break_scale <-
  diff(range(combined_baseline_breaks)) / diff(range(combined_t0_visible_breaks))
combined_baseline_limits <- c(
  combined_baseline_breaks[1] -
    (combined_t0_visible_breaks[1] - combined_t0_limits[1]) *
      combined_baseline_break_scale,
  combined_baseline_breaks[length(combined_baseline_breaks)] +
    (combined_t0_limits[2] - tail(combined_t0_visible_breaks, 1)) *
      combined_baseline_break_scale
)
nest_period_start <- min(found_dates_all_$date_)
nest_period_end <- max(found_dates_all_$date_)

combined_jday_to_label <- function(x) {
  format(combined_origin + round(x) - 1, "%d %b")
}

make_plot_date_lookup <- function(model_obj) {
  dat_plot <- model_obj$data
  n_dates <- max(dat_plot$date_J) - min(dat_plot$date_J) + 1

  tibble(
    date_J = seq(
      from = min(dat_plot$date_J),
      to = max(dat_plot$date_J),
      length.out = n_dates
    ),
    date_J_scaled = seq(
      from = min(dat_plot$date_J_scaled),
      to = max(dat_plot$date_J_scaled),
      length.out = n_dates
    )
  ) %>%
    mutate(date_ = combined_origin + round(date_J - 1))
}

make_population_predictions <- function(model_obj, state_grid) {
  date_lookup <- make_plot_date_lookup(model_obj)

  newdata <- tidyr::crossing(
    date_J_scaled = date_lookup$date_J_scaled,
    state_grid
  ) %>%
    mutate(rings_comb = NA, season = NA) %>%
    left_join(date_lookup, by = "date_J_scaled")

  fitted_vals <- fitted(
    model_obj$fitted_model,
    newdata = newdata,
    re_formula = NA,
    summary = TRUE
  )

  newdata %>%
    mutate(
      fit = fitted_vals[, "Estimate"],
      lower = fitted_vals[, "Q2.5"],
      upper = fitted_vals[, "Q97.5"]
    )
}

make_individual_predictions <- function(model_obj, id_cols, ndraws = 50) {
  date_lookup <- make_plot_date_lookup(model_obj)

  newdata <- tidyr::crossing(
    date_J_scaled = date_lookup$date_J_scaled,
    model_obj$data %>% distinct(across(all_of(id_cols)))
  )

  add_epred_draws(
    model_obj$fitted_model,
    newdata = newdata,
    ndraws = ndraws
  ) %>%
    left_join(date_lookup, by = "date_J_scaled")
}

curve_panel_theme <- function(show_x = FALSE, bottom_margin = 5.5) {
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30", face = "italic"),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "cm"),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, lineend = "round", colour = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, lineend = "round", colour = "grey60"),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = if (show_x) {
      element_text(size = 9, angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, colour = "grey30")
    } else {
      element_blank()
    },
    plot.margin = unit(c(0, -15, bottom_margin, 0), "pt")
  )
}

posterior_panel_theme <- function(show_x = FALSE, bottom_margin = 0) {
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40"),
      axis.title.x = if (show_x) {
        element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey40")
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      axis.text.x = if (show_x) {
        element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", angle = 45, hjust = 1)
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      text = element_text(family = "sans"),
      plot.margin = margin(0, 5.5, bottom_margin, 10)
    )
}

count_individuals_by_state <- function(model_obj, state_col) {
  model_obj$data %>%
    distinct(rings_comb, .data[[state_col]]) %>%
    count(.data[[state_col]], name = "n_ind")
}

make_state_labeler <- function(label_map) {
  function(x) unname(label_map[x])
}

make_halfeye_plot <- function(draws_tbl,
                              fill_values,
                              x_limits,
                              x_breaks,
                              x_title_font = FALSE,
                              x_labels = waiver(),
                              x_title = NULL,
                              show_x = FALSE,
                              state_labels = waiver(),
                              show_y_labels = TRUE,
                              point_shape = 23,
                              bottom_margin = 0) {
  ggplot(draws_tbl, aes(x = estimate, y = state, fill = state)) +
    stat_halfeye(
      .width = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95),
      color = "black",
      point_fill = "white",
      shape = point_shape,
      slab_alpha = 0.75
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(
      limits = rev(names(fill_values)),
      labels = state_labels
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = x_breaks,
      labels = x_labels,
      expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
    ) +
    labs(x = x_title) +
    posterior_panel_theme(show_x = show_x, bottom_margin = bottom_margin) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = if (show_y_labels) {
        element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40")
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      axis.title.x =
        if (x_title_font == "ggtext") {
          ggtext::element_markdown(family = "sans")
        } else if (x_title_font == "normal") {
          element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey40")
        } else if (x_title_font == "none") {
          element_blank()
        }
	    )
	}

make_sex_dodged_baseline_plot <- function(draws_tbl,
                                          state_levels,
                                          fill_values,
                                          x_limits,
                                          x_breaks,
                                          x_title = NULL,
                                          show_x = FALSE,
                                          x_title_font = FALSE,
                                          show_y_labels = FALSE,
                                          bottom_margin = 0) {
  ggplot(
    draws_tbl %>%
      mutate(
        sex = factor(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
        state = factor(state, levels = state_levels)
      ),
    aes(x = estimate, y = state, fill = state, group = interaction(state, sex))
  ) +
    stat_halfeye(
      .width = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95),
      color = "black",
      point_fill = "white",
      shape = 21,
      slab_alpha = 0.75,
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(state_levels)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = x_breaks,
      expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(0.4, length(state_levels) + 1),
      expand = FALSE,
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    labs(x = x_title) +
    posterior_panel_theme(show_x = show_x, bottom_margin = bottom_margin) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = if (show_y_labels) {
        element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40")
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      axis.title.x =
        if (x_title_font == "ggtext") {
          ggtext::element_markdown(family = "sans")
        } else if (x_title_font == "normal") {
          element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey40")
        } else if (x_title_font == "none") {
          element_blank()
        }
    )
}
```
